name: HandBrake
description: HandBrake is a tool for converting video from nearly any format to a selection of modern, widely supported codecs. The graphical user interface (GUI) of the application can be accessed through a modern web browser, requiring no installation or configuration on the client side, or via any VNC client. The container is built against Alpine Linux to provide an efficient image in terms of size and resource usage. A fully automated mode is also available: drop files into a watch folder and let HandBrake process them without any user interaction. For a complete documentation of this container, see https://github.com/jlesage/docker-handbrake#readme

paths.name: Config Directory
paths.description: Stores the application's configuration, state, logs, and any files requiring persistency.

paths.name: Storage
paths.description: Contains files from the host that need to be accessible to the application.

paths.name: Watch Directory
paths.description: The location for videos to be automatically converted.

paths.name: Output Directory
paths.description: The destination for converted video files.

paths.name: Trash Directory
paths.description: When trash usage is enabled, converted source files are moved here instead of being deleted.

ports.name: WEB Port for GUI (Bridge Network Type)
ports.description: Port to access the application's GUI via the web interface. NOTE: This setting is relevant only when the Network Type is set to `Bridge`.

ports.name: VNC Port for GUI (Bridge Network Type)
ports.description: Port to access the application's GUI via VNC protocol. Optional if no VNC client is used. NOTE: This setting is relevant only when the Network Type is set to `Bridge`.

variables.name: User ID
variables.description: ID of the user the application runs as.

variables.name: Group ID
variables.description: ID of the group the application runs as.

variables.name: Umask
variables.description: Mask controlling permissions for newly created files and folders, specified in octal notation.

variables.name: Locale
variables.description: Sets the locale, defining the application's language, if supported. Format is `language[_territory][.codeset]`. For example, Australian English using UTF-8 is `en_AU.UTF-8`.

variables.name: Niceness (priority)
variables.description: Priority at which the application should run. A niceness value of `-20` is the highest, `19` is the lowest and `0` the default. NOTE: Setting a negative value requires additional permissions. Thus, `--cap-add=SYS_NICE` must be added to Extra Parameters (shown when Advanced View is enabled).

variables.name: Display Width
variables.description: Width (in pixels) of the application's window.

variables.name: Display Height
variables.description: Height (in pixels) of the application's window.

variables.name: Dark Mode
variables.description: When set to `1`, enables dark mode for the application.

variables.name: Web Audio
variables.description: When set to `1`, enables audio support, allowing audio produced by the application to play through the browser.

variables.name: Web Host Clipboard Sync
variables.description: When set to `1`, enables support for synchronizing the host system clipboard with the application inside the container. Actual availability still depends on the browser.

variables.name: Web File Manager
variables.description: When set to `1`, enables the web file manager, allowing interaction with files inside the container through a web browser, supporting operations like renaming, deleting, uploading, and downloading.

variables.name: Web File Manager Allowed Paths
variables.description: Comma-separated list of paths within the container that the file manager can access. By default, the container's entire filesystem is not accessible, and this variable specifies allowed paths. If set to `AUTO`, commonly used folders and those mapped to the container are automatically allowed. The value `ALL` allows access to all paths (no restrictions).

variables.name: Web File Manager Denied Paths
variables.description: Comma-separated list of paths within the container that the file manager cannot access. A denied path takes precedence over an allowed path.

variables.name: Web Desktop Notifications
variables.description: When set to `1`, enables the web notification service, allowing the browser to display desktop notifications from the application.

variables.name: Web Terminal
variables.description: When set to `1`, enables access to a terminal from the web interface. It is strongly recommended to configure the container with secure web access (HTTPS).

variables.name: Web Terminal
variables.description: The shell used by the web terminal.

variables.name: Web Authentication
variables.description: When set to `1`, protects the application's GUI with a login page when accessed via a web browser. Access is granted only with valid credentials. Requires secure web access (HTTPS).

variables.name: Web Authentication Allow Insecure
variables.description: When set to `1`, allows web authentication without secure connection (HTTPS). NOT RECOMMENDED. Use only if you fully understand the risks.

variables.name: Web Authentication Token Validity Time
variables.description: Lifetime of a token, in hours. A token is assigned to the user after successful login. As long as the token is valid, the user can access the application's GUI without logging in again. Once the token expires, the login page is displayed again.

variables.name: Web Authentication Username
variables.description: Optional username for web authentication. Provides a quick and easy way to configure credentials for a single user. For more secure configuration or multiple users, see the documentation.

variables.name: Web Authentication Password
variables.description: Optional password for web authentication. Provides a quick and easy way to configure credentials for a single user. For more secure configuration or multiple users, see the documentation.

variables.name: Secure Connection
variables.description: When set to `1`, uses an encrypted connection to access the application's GUI (via web browser or VNC client).

variables.name: Secure Connection VNC Method
variables.description: Method used for encrypted VNC connection. Possible values are `SSL` or `TLS`.

variables.name: Secure Connection Certificate Check Interval
variables.description: Interval, in seconds, at which the system checks if web or VNC certificates have changed. When a change is detected, affected services are automatically restarted. A value of `0` disables the check.

variables.name: Web Listening Port (Non-Bridge Network Type)
variables.description: Port used by the web server to serve the application's GUI. This port is internal to the container and typically does not need to be changed. NOTE: This setting is relevant only when the Network Type is set to something else than Bridge.

variables.name: VNC Listening Port (Non-Bridge Network Type)
variables.description: Port used by the VNC server to serve the application's GUI. This port is internal to the container and typically does not need to be changed. NOTE: This setting is relevant only when the Network Type is set to something else than Bridge.

variables.name: Enable CJK Font
variables.description: When set to `1`, installs the open-source font `WenQuanYi Zen Hei`, supporting a wide range of Chinese/Japanese/Korean characters.

variables.name: HandBrake GUI State
variables.description: Setting this to `1` enables the HandBrake GUI; `0` disables it.

variables.name: HandBrake GUI State
variables.description: Action to be taken on the HandBrake GUI queue at startup. When set to `PROCESS`, HandBrake automatically starts encoding items in the queue. When set to `CLEAR`, the queue is cleared. Any other value results in no action on the queue.

variables.name: Automatic Video Converter: State
variables.description: Setting this to `1` enables the automatic video converter, `0` disables it.

variables.name: Automatic Video Converter: Preset
variables.description: Preset used by the automatic video converter. The preset must be identified in the format `CATEGORY/PRESET NAME`. Available presets can be seen via the HandBrake GUI.

variables.name: Automatic Video Converter: Format
variables.description: Video container format used by the automatic video converter for output files, typically the video filename extension.

variables.name: Automatic Video Converter: Keep Source Files
variables.description: When set to `0`, a successfully converted video is removed from the watch folder.

variables.name: Automatic Video Converter: Video File Extensions
variables.description: Space-separated list of file extensions considered as video files. By default, this list is empty, allowing HandBrake to automatically detect if a file is a video, regardless of its extension (except for extensions defined by `AUTOMATED_CONVERSION_NON_VIDEO_FILE_EXTENSIONS`, which are always considered non-video). This variable is typically unnecessary but useful when only specific video files need conversion.

variables.name: Automatic Video Converter: Non-Video File Action
variables.description: When set to `ignore`, non-video files in the watch folder are ignored. If set to `copy`, non-video files are copied as-is to the output folder.

variables.name: Automatic Video Converter: Non-Video File Extensions
variables.value: jpg jpeg bmp png gif txt nfo
variables.description: Space-separated list of file extensions considered non-video. Most non-video files are properly rejected by HandBrake, but some files, like images, may be convertible despite not being videos.

variables.name: Automatic Video Converter: Watch Directory
variables.description: Path to the watch directory within the container. When set to `AUTO` (the default), the path is set to `/watch` for the first watch directory and `/watchX` for additional ones, where `X` is the index (e.g., `2` for the second).

variables.name: Automatic Video Converter: Output Directory
variables.description: Root directory inside the container where converted videos are written.

variables.name: Automatic Video Converter: Output Subdirectory
variables.description: Subdirectory of the output folder where converted videos are written. By default, videos are saved directly to `/output/`. If set to `Home/Movies`, videos are written to `/output/Home/Movies`. Use `SAME_AS_SRC` to match the source subfolder. For example, if the source is `/watch/Movies/MyMovie/MyMovie.mkv`, the output is written to `/output/Movies/MyMovie/`.

variables.name: Automatic Video Converter: Overwrite Destination
variables.description: When set to `1`, allows overwriting an existing destination file.

variables.name: Automatic Video Converter: Source File Stable Time
variables.description: Time (in seconds) during which properties (e.g., size, time) of a video file in the watch folder must remain unchanged to avoid processing a file being copied.

variables.name: Automatic Video Converter: Minimum Title Duration
variables.description: Minimum title duration (in seconds). Shorter titles are ignored. Applies only to video disc sources (ISO files, `VIDEO_TS` folders, or `BDMV` folders).

variables.name: Automatic Video Converter: Main Title Detection
variables.description: When set to `1`, enables HandBrake's main feature title detection to guess and select the main title. Applies only to video disc sources (ISO files, `VIDEO_TS` folders, or `BDMV` folders).

variables.name: Automatic Video Converter: Check Interval
variables.description: Interval (in seconds) at which the automatic video converter checks for new files.

variables.name: Automatic Video Converter: Number of Watch Folders
variables.description: Maximum number of watch folders handled by the automatic video converter.

variables.name: Automatic Video Converter: Disable Progress in GUI
variables.description: When set to `1`, progress of videos converted by the automatic video converter is not shown in the HandBrake GUI.

variables.name: Automatic Video Converter: Custom HandBrake Arguments
variables.description: Custom arguments to pass to HandBrake during conversion.

variables.name: Automatic Video Converter: Use Trash Directory
variables.description: When set to `1`, the automatic video converter uses the trash directory. This applies only when the converter is configured not to keep source files. In that case, they will be moved to the trash directory (`/trash` inside the container by default) instead of being permanently deleted.

variables.name: Automatic Video Converter: Trash Directory
variables.description: Location of the trash directory inside the container.
